jobs.title: SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
jobs.description:
Job Posting: Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)



Department of Resources Recycling \& Recovery


JC\-526803* 

Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory)
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)
$10,854\.00 \- $13,493\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/31/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory) (EPM I) of the Jurisdiction and Agency Compliance and Enforcement Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) will oversee a unit within Section One. The unit is responsible for compliance and enforcement related to the Integrated Waste Management Act (AB 939\), State Agency and Waste Management Act (AB 75\), Mandatory Commercial Recycling law (AB 341\), Mandatory Commercial Organics Recycling law (AB 1826\), Short\-lived Climate Pollutants law (SB 1383\), and solid waste laws and regulations in the Public Resources Code (PRC) and California Code of Regulations (CCR). The incumbent will provide first line supervision for Environmental Scientist (ES) staff, applying principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, knowledge of statistical methods or analysis, integrated waste management and industry economics, public health, resource management, assessment, review and analysis of technical documents, review and analysis of operations and monitoring records, inspection of businesses, public agencies, solid waste facilities, and public spaces, and enforcement of AB 939, AB 75, AB 341, AB 1826, and SB 1383\. The incumbent will oversee staff’s determination on the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety and the environment for the programs; provide oversight, training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards while also providing technical expertise, training and assistance to staff on evaluation and enforcement matters; review findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensure that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to waste diversion laws. The incumbent accomplishes this by: preparing and reviewing environmental documents to determine the effects of proposed activities on the environment; developing regulations and enforcing environmental and state minimum standards; developing recommendations regarding environmental programs; preparing and editing scientific data to develop environmental policies; reviewing business/facility environmental practices; and consulting with and advising other agencies and institutions engaged in related regulation and investigations.  

  

For more information, please see attached the duty statement.
  

  

**Beginning July 1, 2026, CalRecycle staff will be office\-centered, requiring employees to report to the office at least four days per week.** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program needs. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the positions designated headquarter location, as reflected on the duty statement and at their own expense.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code section 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting eligibility set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location in Sacramento, at their own expense. The EPA headquarters building offices in downtown Sacramento are well\-lit, enclosed, non\-windowed office cubicles in a smoke\-free environment. This position may involve travel throughout California on average 25 percent per month to fulfill field duties and training, which could include consecutive days away from the office and overnight stays. The overnight travel could be over long distances, by car or plane. Work may start outside normal working hours as needed, with advance notice.  

  

Office and field work includes, on a regular basis, writing and reviewing inspection reports and notices, contact with the regulated community by way of in\-person, phone and video conferencing, preparation and review of other documents and internet research. The job occasionally requires you to perform field inspections, hear vehicles and alarms or other audible signals of possible risk.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials / Licensed Asbestos Assessor - Perth, WA
jobs.description:
* Joining our team provides the platform for growing your specialist career
* You’ll be mentored by industry experts and manage projects for our clients
* Perth, WA

  



An excellent opportunity to excel in the profession of Hazardous Materials \& Occupational Hygiene; training and support from highly qualified professionals and a diverse range of projects on offer.

 **Why Join Our Team?**

  

  

Joining our team means you’ll work alongside experienced scientists, engineers, and industry\-leading consultants to deliver a broad range of complex hazardous materials projects.

  

We provide specialist services to several Tier 1 Mining and Oil \& Gas companies, Defence, Federal and State government agencies, and several Tier 1 Mining and Oil \& Gas companies. Our project line\-up includes some of the biggest and most iconic projects in WA and the NT, as well as projects ranging across East Asia, Central Europe and South America.

  



Working closely with the Tetra Tech family of companies, we apply deep technical expertise and project management capability to tackle complex challenges, making sure our solutions are creative, practical and sustainable.

 **About the role**

  

We have a busy project line up right across our national Workplace Health and Safety team and we’re growing the team to keep up!

  

  

In this role, you’ll expand on your knowledge and experience in undertaking hazmat and occupational hygiene site inspections, engaging with clients and contractors, preparing technical reports and managing projects end\-to\-end.  



  

We lead with science and ensure our solutions are tailored to fit each project. The sectors we work in are diverse and span mining, oil \& gas, public infrastructure, future energy, defence and beyond!

  

You will be responsible for:

* Hazardous materials/asbestos assessments and inspections
* Occupational hygiene monitoring and asbestos fibre counting
* Managing field programs for a range of Built Environment investigations
* Observing, guiding, and recording site remediation activities
* Data management, interpretation, and quality assurance/quality control
* Assisting with writing proposals, project correspondence and technical reports

 **About you**

  

To thrive in the role, you'll need:

* Qualifications in related science disciplines and/or occupational hygiene
* Demonstrable experience in the Hazardous Materials and/or Occupational Hygiene field
* Strong project management skills with a focus on quality and delivery
* Great communication, client relationship and teamwork skills
* The ability to travel to regional and country sites as required
* A commitment to safe, environmentally responsible project delivery
* Hold a full Australian driver’s license
* Be an Australian permanent resident or citizen (required for the Department of Defence)

  

Being a Licensed Asbestos Assessor, or eligible to apply within the near future, will be a distinct advantage.

  

This role is likely to include travel and remote work, including shifts away from home.

  

  

**What You’ll Gain:**

* Support and coaching from our Practice Leader and renowned Subject Matter Experts
* Career pathways with opportunities to deepen your technical capability and expand into leadership roles
* A flexible work environment that supports your personal and professional goals
* Access to diverse, high\-profile projects across multiple sectors and geographies, including the possibility for international travel.

 **The Perks You’ll Love:**

* Work\-Life Balance: Flexible work options, tailored hours, study breaks, and the ability to buy extra leave—up to 8 weeks per year!
* Diverse Projects: Work across a wide variety of projects, clients, and sectors
* Growth Opportunities: Professional development, coaching, and mentorship from our top experts
* Memberships: Professional memberships to help you stay ahead in your field
* Recognition: Our reward and recognition program makes sure your hard work doesn’t go unnoticed
* Ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan
* Parental Leave: Paid leave for both primary and secondary caregivers
* Support: Employee assistance program for you and your immediate family
* Travel Discounts: Great deals through our corporate traveller program
* Car Leasing: Take advantage of novated vehicle leasing options

  

**About us**  

  

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high\-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

  

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

  

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global 1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000\+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.

jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description** *"I joined AECOM for the opportunity to work on meaningful, ANZ\-wide projects with awesome people, and I’ve stayed because the opportunities to grow my career and leadership experience." Lauren Spring, Environment Manager \- Western Australia*


AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.


Join AECOM's Geosciences and Remediation Services team in Perth at an exciting time of investment and growth. Backed by a strong pipeline of work across Defence, Mining, Aviation and Oil \& Gas, you'll have the opportunity to lead complex, high\-profile projects, help shape the future of the business, and collaborate with technical specialists across Australia and New Zealand. It's a chance to make a real impact while building your career with one of the world's leading infrastructure consulting firms.

**What will a day in this role look like:**

* Oversee all aspects of project management, including planning, budgeting, financial management, scheduling, quality reviews, and communication with relevant stakeholders.
* Prepare and review technical reports, and other project documentation, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and consistency.
* Lead and manage contaminated sites projects, building and maintaining strong relationships by understanding their needs and delivering high\-quality outcomes.
* Support business development efforts by identifying opportunities, preparing proposals.
* Provide guidance and mentorship to junior team members.

 **Qualifications** **The qualities that help you thrive**


The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

* A degree in environmental science, geology, hydrogeology, chemistry or environmental engineering, along with a current driver’s licence.
* Extensive experience in contaminated land assessment and remediation, with a strong track record in managing projects from start to finish.
* Confident working directly with clients, with the ability to build relationships and provide clear, expert advice.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a knack for explaining technical concepts in a straightforward way.
* Willing to travel for fieldwork across WA and beyond; familiarity with WA regulations and experience on mining or oil and gas sites will be highly regarded.

 **Additional Information** **Why you’ll love working with us**

* Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times, job\-sharing and hybrid work options
* Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave per year
* Swap public holidays – swap Easter or other holidays for ones that suit you better
* Continuous learning and growth \- lunch and learns, professional development courses, financial study assistance, 5 days paid study leave, global career opportunities

Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
